question: Can the dense projections of a two-to-eight-row Gemma 4 verify block run on the one-row decode kernel, faster and bit-identical to decode?
model: Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it UD-Q4_K_XL target, mtp-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-Q8_0 assistant head, BF16 KV
change: Raw gguf_q8_0 projections that ship the T16 tiles allocation run 2-8 rows on the one-row T16 GEMV (one grid row per input row) instead of the T16 WMMA prefill (production) or the exact pack8 prefill (strict). A call that asked for WMMA keeps it above four rows of an output wider than 4608.

kernel_microbench_us.method: scratch microbench, events around five passes over every layer of the shape (cold weights), bf16 activations, W7900
kernel_microbench_us.exact_pack8_note: kernel trace of a five-row exact verify block: gguf_k_pack8_prefill_out_kernel 8.50 ms over 124 launches; the T16 GEMV route 5.37 ms over 117 launches in the production block

row_equality: exact verify bitwise equal to one-token steps at 3, 5, 7 and 9 rows after prompts of 120, 600 and 1100 tokens (72 of 72); in production, rows of 3-row blocks after the 120-token prompt are now bitwise equal as well (envelope KL elsewhere at most 8.8e-2, no argmax change in 72 rows)

verify_block_ms_median.method: scratch timing loop: 25 repetitions after a 600-token prompt, first 5 dropped, rewind between repetitions, production profile
verify_block_ms_median.note: the exact one-row block and decode step read 15.5/16.2 ms in the first phase of this run (clock warm-up); a one-row block is the same code in both settings

public_path.timing_scope: whole public call including prefill of short prompts, 128 greedy tokens; plain call first, then MTP; nothing else running

limitations: Whole-call timing is not isolated decode throughput.
The dense branch runs concurrently with the expert branch, so a five-row production block moved 27.8 -> 27.0 ms although its dense kernel time fell 9.8 -> 5.4 ms.
One-token decode is unchanged (rows == 1 already took this kernel); a prefill chunk of 2-8 rows also takes it.
